q1_issues.issue: The agent-nominalization capability atom (Inheritance producer (can produce)) is not licensed here: the instruction set fires it only for a symbol fused from the surface or for a copular predicate, and explicitly lists an appositive as a merely referring use where you type the referent and stop.

"one of the world's largest producers of softwood" is rendered as the comparison-class (Degree ... (forKind producer)), which means only "large for a producer" rather than "among the largest in the world", and the "world's" possessor/domain restriction is dropped entirely.

The produced amount is put on the event as (Measure sk_produce_1 quantity ... board_foot_per_year) with an unstated scale symbol and a rate unit, and the produce event carries no Patient/Theme at all for what is produced.

q2_gaps: "one of the [superlative] Ns" — a partitive over a superlative set; Most is unique-superlative only, forKind is the norm-for-a-class construction, and Partitives covers quantified subjects rather than a predicative appositive

a measure-phrase direct object of an event ("produce about 7.6 billion board feet a year") — Measure puts a magnitude on an entity's stated dimension, and there is no licensed scale or per-year rate-unit form for an event's output quantity
the possessive "the world's" scoping over a superlative comparison set (a domain restriction, not a possessed thing)
notes: The Can/event core, the "about" hedge (sigma = 10% of 7.6e9) and the (Of weyerhaeuser softwood) nominalization argument are all per spec. The scale symbol `quantity` is an argument term rather than a head, so it is listed as a licence stretch above rather than an unlicensed head.
